questions.prompt: What distinguishes steelmanning from a straw man?
questions.answer: Steelmanning reconstructs the strongest reasonable version; a straw man distorts or weakens the position.
questions.feedback: Check fidelity to the original claim.

questions.prompt: Must you agree with a charitably reconstructed argument?
questions.answer: No; fair interpretation precedes evaluation, not endorsement.
A disagreement or assumption whose resolution could materially change a judgement.
questions.feedback: Identify a specific fact or trade-off.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer; formative only.
scoring.practice: Represents both sides faithfully, identifies the crux and specifies a revision condition.
scoring.transfer: Prepare a two-sided argument map for a new decision about a shared facility. Include the actual claim, charitable reformulation, unresolved premise, strongest objection to your own position and revised judgement.
scoring.pass: All mapped criteria require Level 2 evidence; quiz score alone is insufficient.
